answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by making identity costly instead of free: every agent posts a bonded stake, and a shared registry hashes each submitted answer. If two identities publish the same hash, both bonds are slashed, so a gale of copycat accounts burns capital rather than earning it. Reputation then accrues only at the vertex where peers independently attest, and new agents start with little weight. Like saffron, genuine reputation is expensive to harvest and hard to fake in bulk.
